name: etsh
desc: Two ports of /bin/sh from V6 UNIX (circa 1975)
why: Two ports of the 1975 Sixth Edition Unix shell let you run a living piece of computing history in a terminal.

brief.what_it_is: Etsh is a set of ports of the original V6 UNIX Thompson shell (/bin/sh from V6 UNIX, May 1975), maintained by J.A. Neitzel. The homepage describes two shells: etsh, an enhanced but backward-compatible port, and tsh, an unenhanced port. It also describes glob, a port of the V6 global command. The homepage says nothing about what osh or sh6 are, though both appear among the installed executables. You run it in a terminal as an ordinary interactive shell, and it runs shell scripts and command files written in the V6 Thompson shell language.
brief.why_it_exists: The project exists to preserve and run the 1975 Thompson shell so people can use it. The homepage frames it as UNIX history: "Two ports of the 1975 Sixth Edition Unix shell let you run a living piece of computing history in a terminal" is the brew scout note, and the site adds a History section and a link list for UNIX history.
brief.how_it_works: The shells are ports of the V6 Thompson shell's command language, which the homepage calls a predecessor and subset of the Bourne and C shell languages. The Thompson shell supports pipelines (| or ^), sequential and asynchronous commands (; and &), I/O redirection, globbing, and $1-style parameter substitution. The utilities if, goto, and fd2 are built into etsh and are external programs for tsh. The homepage gives no further internals.
brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, the homepage describes source tarballs (etsh-5.4.0.tar.gz or .tar.xz) with SHA512 checksums and signify signatures, signed by the author's signify key, which is published on the site. It also lists an etsh-current development branch in CVS. No runtime, account, or configuration requirements appear on the homepage. Example RC files are linked for configuring etsh interactively, but I did not open them.
brief.standout: It is a faithful revival of a 1975 shell rather than a reimagining, and it ships both a strict port (tsh) and an enhanced one (etsh) so you can run the original behavior or a backward-compatible upgrade. The author also publishes a gopher hole alongside the web site and signs releases with signify.
brief.status: Apparently maintained. The homepage gives copyright 2003-2025, lists release 5.4.0 with signed checksums, says the author develops and maintains the project, and asks users to try the latest release before reporting bugs. No release date appears on the homepage, and I did not check a changelog or repository.
brief.caveats: The brew description says ports of /bin/sh from V6 UNIX, but the homepage does not say which platforms are supported. Only etsh and tsh are described in detail, and the brew executables list also includes osh, sh6, and glob-related names that the homepage does not explain. I did not follow the Usage, Sources, or NOTES pages, so there are no verified commands and no details on the dialect differences from modern shells. UNIX is a trademark of The Open Group, which the site notes.
quotes: The Etsh Project provides 2 ports of the original /bin/sh from V6 UNIX, May 1975.
Bug reports are certainly welcome, but please try upgrading to the latest release before reporting any bug as it may have already been fixed.
I, J.A. Neitzel, develop and maintain this project, and I sign releases & snapshots of it with the signify key pair declared on the Etsh Signify Key page.
fetch_log: https://etsh.dev/ — fetched OK. The page is a project site, not a GitHub repo, so no README was returned. I did not follow the Usage, Sources, NOTES, or Docs links, so commands and build details are missing.

judge.reason: A runnable, faithful 1975 shell offers a hands-on look at a command language that predates Bourne and C shells, not just a historical writeup.

entry.title: etsh
entry.tldr: Ports of the 1975 Sixth Edition UNIX Thompson shell that run as ordinary interactive shells, so you can type at the ancestor of sh.
entry.deeper_look:
Etsh is a set of ports of the original /bin/sh from V6 UNIX, May 1975, maintained by J.A. Neitzel. That shell was written by Ken Thompson, and the project site calls its language a predecessor and subset of the Bourne and C shell languages. There are two shells. etsh is an enhanced but backward-compatible port. tsh is the unenhanced one. The site also describes glob, a port of the V6 global command.

The Thompson shell is small. It has pipelines (written | or ^), sequential and asynchronous commands (; and &), I/O redirection, globbing, and $1-style parameter substitution. The utilities if, goto, and fd2 are built into etsh and are external programs under tsh. Control flow in this shell is done with those utilities rather than built-in syntax, so scripts read quite differently from modern ones.

The idea underneath is that the shells most people use grew out of this one. Running it shows what was there at the start and what later shells added. You can also run old V6-style command files as they were written.

The homepage does not explain what osh and sh6 are, though both are installed. The project also has a gopher hole, and releases are signed with signify.

entry.whats_unique: It is a faithful revival of a 1975 shell rather than a reimagining. It ships both a strict port (tsh) and a backward-compatible enhanced one (etsh), so you can compare them.
entry.caveats: The homepage does not say which platforms are supported or what osh and sh6 are, and the dialect differs from modern shells, so expect old-style scripting.
